findings.evidence: CL5 says PD12's scan for the name createHash under src/lib/server/codes/ means that 'no code path there can compute a plain hash of anything, a code included'. That is not true. Node 24.22.3 (package.json engines) has the one-shot crypto.hash('sha256', data), which never uses the name createHash. crypto.subtle.digest does not either. And PD12 explicitly says an import of a name never counts, so `import { createHash as h } from 'node:crypto'; h('sha256')` leaves no countable createHash name at all. A plain SHA-256 of a code could therefore land in codes/ with the OB108 check still green.
findings.fix: For this one scan, check the module's imports from crypto instead of a single name. Every import from 'node:crypto' or 'crypto' under src/lib/server/codes/ must name only createHmac, randomBytes and timingSafeEqual (import specifiers count here; a namespace or default import of crypto is refused). The names hash, subtle, webcrypto and digest must not appear. Restate the CL5 sentence and the OB108 row to match.
findings.path: section 7 CL5 and section 4 PD12 (createHash scan); section 2 row OB108

findings.evidence: Step 5 accepts a class only when its owner_id is the redeeming user. So every redemption into a given class comes from one user, and the user's code_attempt_limits row, taken FOR UPDATE in step 4 and held until commit, already makes them run one at a time. T2's test runs eight redeemWithin calls for one owner into one class. They never reach the class lock concurrently, so 'eight distinct numbers and no error' would also pass on a build without step 5's FOR NO KEY UPDATE. The trace also says 'each takes the class row ... so they queue', which is not the lock that actually does the queuing. The class lock really matters against ST5's staff move, which takes no account lock and is deferred.
findings.fix: Say in T2 that, in Phase 2, redemption against redemption into one class is serialized by the account lock, and why. Then prove the class lock directly, as T1(b) does for the code row: an owner connection holds the class row FOR NO KEY UPDATE, the redemption is shown waiting in pg_locks, and it finishes with the right display number once the lock is released. Add the redemption-against-move case to ST6 (T8 or a T2 variant) for jade-pe9.
